issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g. lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, etc.) but the constructor, getters/setters, and other methods use camelCase names (e.g. lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This name mismatch makes the solution class uncompilable and conflicts with the attribute names shown in the problem UML and described in the task, preventing students from using the solution as a correct reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute names consistent between declarations and usage. Update the field declarations to use the camelCase names shown in the problem statement and used throughout the class (e.g. private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; private int numberOfGuestStudents; private int numberOfLecturers; private int numberOfTutors;), or alternatively change all constructor and method references to the declared snake_case fields. Preferably align fields to the UML/camelCase naming to match the rest of the code and the exercise description.

issues.description: The problem statement / UML specify attributes using camelCase names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), but the solution implementation declares these fields using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors). This creates a mapping disconnect for students (they expect the camelCase fields from the UML) and also leads to internal inconsistency in the solution where the constructor and methods reference camelCase names (e.g. this.lectureName) that do not match the declared snake_case fields, which can cause compilation errors and confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Align identifier names across artifacts. Change the field declarations in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java (solution) to use the camelCase names from the UML: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors. Ensure the constructor, getters, setters and all methods reference these same field names. Prefer camelCase to follow Java conventions and match the problem statement.
